Evelyn,

Hope you had a good weekend. Our renewal for Q3 is coming up and we want to avoid the uncertainty of year-over-year list increases given our product roadmap dependencies. We're exploring a multi-year prepay to lock unit pricing for the term. High level ask: a 3-year commitment with annual prepay installments (paid at start of each year) and a protective pricing collar so list increases don't affect our committed rate.

Key constraints on our side:
- We need predictable unit cost for budgeting and a simple ramp (20% year 1, 40% year 2, 40% year 3 is what finance prefers).
- We prefer annual invoices to match fiscal cycles (no huge upfront lump sum).
- We require minimal contract redlines and prefer standard SOW + PO flow.

Can you share examples/options you typically offer for this? Also, what discount bands and protections you can offer tied to annual prepay vs full upfront prepay?

Thanks,
Liam

Evelyn / Marissa / Liam — attaching three scenarios that map to the ask. Short summary in-line below and the attached workbook has the line-item math.

Attachment: 2027-04-19_Renewal_Term_Scenarios.xlsx (stub)

Scenario A — Annual prepay (your preferred flow)
- 3-year term, annual prepay at start of each year
- Yearly prepay discount: 10% off list for year 1 (paid at start), 8% year 2, 6% year 3 (effective blended ~8%)
- Pricing collar: list increases capped at 5% year-over-year for the committed units
- Ramp: supports 20/40/40 via staged credit allocations (we invoice annual prepay; credits applied monthly against usage)

Scenario B — Hybrid (smaller upfront + annual top-ups)
- 30% upfront prepay (year 1), then annual prepay for years 2–3
- Upfront discount: 12% on the upfront slice; annual slices receive 7%/5% discounts
- Pricing collar: 3% cap; stronger cash upfront gives better protection

Scenario C — Full upfront 3-year prepay
- Full prepay at signing; 14% flat discount across term; pricing locked with no list pass-through for committed units
- Best unit economics but requires Acme to accept one payment at signing

Notes/risks:
- If Acme needs annual invoices only (PO), Scenario A is simplest but gives smaller discount vs full upfront.
- Collar mechanics can be implemented as an explicit contract schedule or via a simple amendment that references the model catalog at signing.

Next steps: Liam — which of the three aligns with Acme's treasury preferences? Marissa and I can then draft the SOW/term summary and get legal looped for a short amendment.

Thanks,
